summary: ASTER EARA, developed by Arkham Orbit, is an experimental aerospace health-monitoring platform designed for crewed space missions. It combines environmental telemetry such as oxygen, CO₂, pressure, temperature, humidity, radiation, and life-support efficiency with crew signals including heart rate, SpO₂, respiratory rate, sleep, fatigue, stress, cognition, and blood-pressure proxies. Neural-network models analyze recent history to forecast potential changes up to 24 hours in advance, while a daily model identifies accumulated sleep loss, fatigue, and mental workload. The system uses an energy-aware interface: it keeps essential monitoring active with minimal visual processing and switches to a detailed mode only when an anomaly requires attention. Alerts include context, affected body regions, trends, and configurable self-care guidance. ASTER EARA addresses communication delays, limited spacecraft resources, and the need to act before a situation becomes critical. The demonstration uses synthetic mission data based on NASA references and is intended for research and visualization, not clinical diagnosis.
details:
ASTER EARA is an experimental predictive health-monitoring platform designed for crews operating in isolated space environments. It combines environmental telemetry—including oxygen, CO₂, cabin pressure, temperature, humidity, radiation, gravity, and life-support efficiency—with crew information such as heart rate, respiratory rate, SpO₂, blood-pressure proxies, sleep, fatigue, stress, cognition, hydration, and ECG summaries.

The system maintains a continuous mission timeline and analyzes both current conditions and historical trends. A neural-network model uses 168 hours of hourly observations to forecast possible changes during the next 24 hours. A second daily model analyzes 31 days of history to identify accumulated sleep loss, fatigue, mental workload, and pressure-related trends. An additional event detector demonstrates how a critical synthetic event can be identified before its labelled onset.

ASTER EARA is also designed for resource-constrained spacecraft. Its energy-saving mode keeps essential monitoring active while reducing unnecessary animations, charts, and visual updates. When a significant anomaly is detected, the interface switches to a detailed mode with trends, alert context, a 3D anatomical model, affected body regions, and configurable self-care guidance.

The intended impact is to help crews recognize emerging risks earlier, reduce information overload, preserve onboard resources, and support human decision-making when communication with Earth is delayed. The system does not replace medical professionals and does not autonomously administer treatment or change spacecraft systems.

The project was developed with Python, PyTorch, NumPy, pandas, FastAPI, Uvicorn, React, TypeScript/JavaScript, Vite, Three.js, HTML, CSS, PowerShell, Git, and Git LFS preparation. It runs locally on standard Windows hardware and can use CPU or GPU resources depending on the available computer.

Our creative approach combines predictive neural networks, environmental monitoring, energy-aware interface design, temporal replay, and an anatomical 3D visualization in one system. The demonstration uses a reproducible ten-year synthetic mission scenario based on NASA reference sources and public physiological data structures. We clearly separate official references from synthetic crew data and treat all predictions as experimental research outputs rather than clinical diagnoses.
